testing.note: Mamavation's plastic sandwich bag study, EPA certified lab, updated February 2025, found Ziploc Sandwich Bags and Ziploc Slider Power Shield 15 gallon storage bags non-detect for organic fluorine at a 10 ppm detection limit. Thirteen other bags in the same round did indicate PFAS, up to 34 ppm. That is a clean PFAS result with its limit stated; it says nothing about what polyethylene itself gives up to fat and heat, which is the materials check.

materials.source: https://kinderfeets.com/products/balance-bike-black-03619 : "Handmade with sustainable wood from fast-growing birch trees", "Painted with non-toxic, water-based black paint", "non-toxic grips", "non-formaldehyde glue", "Suitable for ages 2 years and older". https://kinderfeets.com/pages/frequently-asked-questions : "Kinderfeets products are made using fast-growing bamboo, eco-friendly birch wood, and FSC-certified German beechwood", "EVA Airless Tyres also ensure safety", "water-based paints and lacquers". The grips are called non-toxic and never named, which is a word rather than a material (rule 3.4), so they are the undisclosed part under 3.7. The EVA tyres run on the floor and are not in the path a rider touches, so they are noted and not counted under 3.4. Age 2 and over, so this is not a mouthed product. Checked on 2026-09-19 whether any balance bike names its grips, because a flag that fires on a whole category tells a shopper nothing (rule 3.6). Eight brands, and not one names a grip material that would pass. Early Rider names theirs and the answer is "SOFT TOUCH EVA FOAM" with an "EVA PAD" saddle (us.earlyrider.com/products/lite-wooden-balance-bike-toddler, earlyrider.com/products/replacement-orginal-handlebar-grips: "black EVA foam handlebar grips"). woom's GO 1 describes its grips and saddle cover by function only. Wishbone says "black grips" on the bike page and names nothing on the grips page itself. Puky gives a "foam rubber" saddle and no grip material. Banwood publishes no materials. Trybike's own pages name none; only retailers say rubber. So the caution here is a disclosure gap across the category rather than a fault unique to this bike.

testing.note: Searched Lead Safe Mama, Mamavation and Consumer Reports on 2026-09-19. No independent test of a Kinderfeets bike has been published. The maker names CE, ASTM, EN71 and AS/NZS 8124, which are the toy safety standards every children's product sold here has to meet, covering things like small parts and sharp edges. They are a floor, not a measurement of what the EVA gives off.
